pillars.name: Building in Public
pillars.description: Share what you're actually building this week — progress, decisions, a screenshot-worthy moment.
pillars.notesPrompt: What did you build, ship, or decide this week? Give 2-5 real bullets (a feature, a customer conversation, a hard call you made).
hooks: I shipped something small this week that taught me something big.
Here's what building {topic} actually looked like this week — no highlight reel.
Nobody tells you this part of building a business:
A year ago I couldn't have done this. This week I did.
Progress update: {topic}.
structure: Open with the hook
1-2 sentences of real context (what you were trying to do)
What actually happened — the specific, concrete detail from your notes
The lesson or shift in thinking it caused
One line inviting a reply or opinion from the reader
ctas: What are you building right now? Drop it below.
Curious how others are tackling this — thoughts?
Following along? I'll share the next step soon.

pillars.name: Money & Wealth Mindset
pillars.description: A genuine lesson about how you think about money, risk, or wealth — grounded in something real, not a claim about results you haven't earned.
pillars.notesPrompt: What real belief about money or risk did you test, confirm, or drop this week? Give 2-5 honest bullets — a decision, a fear you faced, a number you looked at.
hooks: The way I think about money changed the day I did this:
Nobody talks about this side of chasing financial independence.
A mindset shift that cost me nothing and changed everything:
I used to think {topic}. I was wrong.
Wealth isn't just a number. Here's what I mean:
structure: Open with the hook
The specific moment or decision that prompted the reflection
What you believed before, and what changed it
The principle you're taking forward — stated plainly, without overpromising
One line inviting discussion
ctas: What's a money belief you've had to unlearn?
What would you add to this?

pillars.name: Lessons Learned
pillars.description: A specific mistake or hard-won lesson from the past week, told honestly.
pillars.notesPrompt: What went wrong or harder than expected this week, and what did it teach you? Give 2-5 bullets.
hooks: This mistake cost me time this week. Here's what I'd tell my past self:
I got this wrong. Here's the lesson.
The hard way I learned {topic}:
Three days ago I made a call I'd make differently today.
structure: Open with the hook
What you attempted and what went wrong, stated plainly
The real cause, not the polished version
What you're changing because of it
One line inviting others to share their version
ctas: What's a lesson that cost you before it taught you?
Anyone else learn this one the hard way?

pillars.name: Wins & Milestones
pillars.description: A real, specific win — sized honestly, credited to the work that produced it.
pillars.notesPrompt: What actually went right this week? Give 2-5 bullets with real specifics (a number, a name, a date) — no rounding up.
hooks: Small win, but I'm taking it: {topic}.
This took longer than I expected, but it happened.
Milestone update — here's exactly what got us here:
Not a huge win. Still a real one.
structure: Open with the hook
The specific, verifiable detail of the win
The unglamorous work that actually produced it
Who or what helped along the way (credit generously)
One line inviting others to share their own wins
ctas: What's a win you're proud of this week, even a small one?
Tag someone who helped you get somewhere this month.

pillars.name: Behind the Scenes
pillars.description: The unglamorous, ordinary reality of a specific day or task — the opposite of a highlight reel.
pillars.notesPrompt: What did an ordinary hour or task actually look like this week? Give 2-5 bullets of plain, specific detail.
hooks: What building {topic} actually looks like on a Tuesday:
Here's the unfiltered version of this week:
No highlight reel today. Just what actually happened.
The boring part of the job, honestly:
structure: Open with the hook
A plain, specific walk-through of the real task or hour
Why the unglamorous part matters more than it looks
One honest takeaway
One line inviting others to share their 'boring' reality
ctas: What does your unfiltered Tuesday look like?
Anyone else find the boring part is where the real work happens?
